Before I shopped at Felgenoutlet I made a big mistake shopping at a small independent online seller in Germany. I was sold wheels I could not get TUV certification for. The seller made it impossible to return the wheels. It ended with hiring a lawyer to get my money back and is ongoing. I wish I had have gone to Felgenoutlet first. Here is why. 1. They quickly and professionally answered my questions 2. TUV certified Wheels and include all the necessary paperwork for your car. Fit for your car with TUV papers CONFIRMED. 3. Lightning fast delivery 4. Included FREE Wheel bolts and center rings! 5. Competitive pricing. 6. Multi language support - email and phone! For people who are from outside of Germany and may not know how TUV works here are some things you must know: If you are changing wheels on your car they MUST be TUV certified. If you are driving around on wheels without tuv certification and get into an accident you will have NO insurance coverage and be in a world of trouble, even when its NOT your fault. It is NOT worth the risk. When shopping for wheels be sure to look for TUV certified sellers ONLY. DO NOT shop with any seller that does not have this! Felgenoutlet is one of the TOP sellers of wheels in Germany. They know the certification requirements and law. They will make sure what you are buying is 100% legal for your car. They will inform you if there are any concerns or mistakes. Shopping at Felgenoutlet you know what you are getting is quality tuv approved and will keep you safe and legal. Only 2 things went wrong: They sent the wrong Hub Centric Rings. I ordered 64-54.1 and I got 64-56.6 instead. I was told I would get the correct ones mailed to me. They never arrived so I had to go purchase my own. This was frustrating as it delayed my installation. When the packages arrived some of them where badly damaged. I went through every package with the DPD guy and everything was OK. It just looked bad, Very poorly packaged for shipping wheels. But do keep in mind they came strait from the manufacture (Tec) and not Felgenoutlet. The Wheels arrived super fast! 3 working days but because they came from the manufacture I was not provided with any shipping or tracking info. I would like to see this change in the future. Despite these small issues I would say you can shop with confidence here. Its safe legal and legit. UPDATE: After reading my issues almost a month later Felgenoutlet sent me the correct center rings and also sent me a free care package with wheel cleaning tools! I did not expect that. That is good customer service! I hope this helped you good luck.

supplier_response: Hello Nour, Thank you for your review! We are sorry to hear that you had a bad experience at AUTODOC. We have checked your order and could see that you have ordered a spare part marked ''core part''. When you purchase such spare parts you have to pay a core charge in addition to the price of the spare part itself. According to European legislation, the core charge is the amount that the manufacturer requires as a deposit to guarantee the old spare part is returned for remanufacturing. The core charge is refunded when the old spare part is returned. This information can be easily found on our website under ''Core Exchange'' or ''Stomavgift'' for the Swedish version of our site. Also there it is stated that the return of the old part is to be made at the customer's expenses. Thank you for your understanding! Best regards, Autodoc Team

This review is for the company Autodoc or autoteiledirekt.de (they seem to operate under a bunch of different names, so I posted here and on Autodoc reviews). The short version: Absolutely terrible customer service, bordering on a scam. Order somewhere else! The very long one for those who care: I ordered a bunch of parts from them and to be fair the items are what I expected and do their jobs but 2 days after the items were supposed to be at my house (shipped inside Germany so no excuse there) I called them up and after pretty unfriendly interaction with their customer service guy I got promised that it would go out that day. So, if it says 2 days, expect a week. While I was talking to him I noticed the parts where now 30 Euros cheaper on a 200 Euro order and I asked him for a deal. I would have taken store credit, even a complimentary sponge or a packet of gummy bears or something that showed any interest in their customers, but he wasn't willing to budge. Fair enough there too, they don't have to. So, I told him I would just order the stuff again and return the first package and since they already delivered the parts too late for me I had all the time in the world (second package was late by the same time frame too). I even bought their safe order (sicher bestellen) feature on the first order, which states that I can return the uninstalled parts for a full refund for any reason within a 100 days or something like that. Since the boxes are just sitting here and haven’t even been opened it shouldn't have been a problem. A week after I filed for the return I haven't even gotten a mail saying that it is being processed other than their automated instant reply so I called them up again. I didn’t even get an answer the first 4 times I called even though it kept telling me constantly I was next in line. After 15 Minutes and 27 Seconds you get dropped from the line each time so you get to try again. I have a headset and plenty of time while i was doing other things so I just kept calling. Even tried calling them from 3 lines at once (I got bored) and you get the same message on all of them. That was around 10am on a regular business day. Never got through to anyone then so I tried again in the afternoon and after the second round of waiting I actually got someone who couldn't even say hello or good bye or anything and I tried my best to be extra friendly. I got some results in the form of six emails (one for each part I ordered) saying my return was accepted and an attached PDF Return Form for every part. Seemed like progress but it also said that my return mailers would come in separate emails which still haven't arrived 5 days later. I guess I will listening to some more annoying music and automated messages next week. At this point I fully expect them to either not answer at all or at best be extremely rude again. Chances of me getting the full refund, that their extra safe order service promises are slim to none and I bet they will give me the full runaround for that too. Calling it what it is at this point is a Scam. I will change this review accordingly if they manage to surprise me and not do any of that, after all terrible service and late deliveries aren't a scam if the parts are what you bought but at this point it sure looks like a Scam when it comes to their return policies and safe order options. Update (26.06.2018): I guess complaining loudly on the internet does help since their english speaking customer service called me up first thing monday and sent me the return mailer (just one though even though I got two boxes but since they already had all the heavy stuff in one box and the 2 super light things in a seperate one I figured they might as well go in a single box. Didn't want to argue over this but I took a bunch of pictures anyway). The english speaking customer service rep was very nice, which was a welcome change so I guess I'll be carefully optimistic and wait. Update (09.07.2018): Turns out they actually did send me three labels - in yet again three separate emails - just two ended up in spam. I guess since it took 40something emails (not even kidding) to get to this point. So I sent the three packages in the same arrangement they came here and apparently they received them on Jul. 2nd. Still waiting to hear anything further. Don't hold your breath on getting your money in any sort of timely fashion back. Mind you I started the Process over a month ago on June 3rd. I do realize the return proves and banks and all that take their sweet time too. I don't have a problem with that, but this is just ridiculous. How does a company with that terrible of a customer service stay in business these days? I've head better customer service from Indian tech support scammers than these guys. I’m curious what happens next. My guess is I do get some money back at some point or another but not even close to the amount I paid with all kinds of bogus charges and “service” fees as a justification. I guess we will see.

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend dackonline.se based on my experience. I ordered a complete set of winter wheels on November 9th, with a promised delivery time of a maximum of 14 working days. This deadline passed by several weeks without me receiving any clear explanation. During this period, I was given conflicting information every time I called customer service – sometimes they claimed the tires couldn’t be delivered and tried to get me to cancel the order, while other times they promised that the wheels would be shipped “this week or next week.” None of it was true. At the same time, the exact same wheel package continued to be shown as “available” on their website, which felt both misleading and unprofessional. The customer service by phone cannot make any decisions at all; they only act as intermediaries and constantly refer to “the other department” that responds by email. This creates a Catch-22 situation – the phone support can’t help, and the email support doesn’t reply in time. Now they have also informed me that the product I ordered is sold out, despite it being listed as available during my entire waiting period. I have been forced to try to solve the issue myself, contact the Consumer Agency, and argue for an alternative, even though the fault lies entirely with them. It is extremely frustrating as a customer to have to chase answers, be transferred around, and receive different information with every contact. Especially when winter tires are legally required in Sweden and you depend on receiving your delivery on time. I recommend buying from a more reliable supplier that can actually keep their delivery times and provide consistent information to their customers.

supplier_response: Dear customer, Thank you very much for your detailed explanation. We are truly sorry to hear that your experience with our delivery and customer service has been so disappointing. We fully understand how frustrating this situation must be for you, especially given the urgent need for the parts and the costs you are incurring as a result. According to the applicable procedures, we can only process a refund or a new shipment after the damaged package has been returned and received by us. supplier_response: Hello Noel, thank you for the feedback. We will explain you the situation. We have no influence on the customs clearance process. Unfortunately, there may be delays of a few days. UPS was demonstrably contacted by us and the refund was already made beginning of May. We offered you support since our aim is that you have completely functional product. There are occasional vehicles where the RaceChip does not achieve the expected results although it is individually designed and programmed for the engine. It must be pointed out here that identical engines can have a different serial dispersion due to manufacturing tolerances. If the engine differs too much from the standard it can happen in exceptional cases that the RaceChip does not harmonize perfectly right away. The engine's general condition does also play an important role in relation to chiptuning. If the engine does not perform like expected with the RaceChip our customers can always contact our technical support. Usually they can match the tuning software afterwards in order to achieve the expected results in the end. In case the final results should still not meet the expectations we refund payment. Best regards, Your RaceChip-Team

supplier_response: Hello Roy, please contact our technical support team like you already did when you were satisfied in first place: https://www.racechip.com/service-support/customer-support.html Engines have different serial tolerances, which means that the performance numbers of the maker is not always the real performance of the motor. The performance increase includes a tolerance of up to 8%. The performance also changes depending on the mileage of the engine. Depending on the power distribution of the engine, there is a different power delta. This means that the maximum power of the respective motor is achieved even on different mappings. That is the reason for the different mappings. Best regards, Your RaceChip-Team

I realise being in the UK we are not part of Europe but only fedex seem to impose these charges, so maybe consider another courier instead and send as a gift.

Well....got a GTS for my Suzuki Swift (AZ) Boosterjet Sport 2019. No problems at all installing it (after I got the right pictures for my car - K14C engine). But........I can´t connect it between mobile phone (Android 7) and the GTS. It fails big time and following messege came up: "Attension. Error adding a new product. Try again". Yup. Did that 10-12 times now and still no succes. Waiting answer from support. I got help and it works.....for now

review_text: Purchased the “S” version for my Audi A3 1.9TDI. Simple to install, great price and instantly noticeable increase in torque. I’m yet to test it on a long run to check whether the MPG improves. So far, so good.

Got the GTS for my 2020 MINI JCW. Installation was breeze easy, clear instruction with more than enough cable ties included. May want to include velcro tape next time, RaceChip. Tried all stages, got mine with the apps control, all suits my driving style depending whenever I need it. I look forward in getting the XLR for quick throttle response next :)

Easy to install the chip, the instructions for the product were clear and came with pictures. The performance you can feel it more on setup number 5, the setup number 3 that comes straight out of the box doesn't make much difference from standard setup.

I was forced to file a complaint with the gendarmerie for fraud following my purchase. The box is incompatible with my engine. All tests and instructions were followed. After 2 cases changed, I asked for a refund. They sent me back a third. I had someone from customer service explain to me that they didn't care about my problem, that I didn't have to return them and that I could go and file a complaint. TO FIRE, THEY ARE SCAMS !! And following this review, know that RACECHIP will contact Trustpilot to let them know that I am not a customer so that my review is not published. Unfortunately for them, I kept all the credentials and Trustpilot and a completely neutral and objective site. I hope you don’t make the same mistake I did.
supplier_response: Dear Julien , thanks for your feedback. This description is very unusual. It seems like our Customer Service is already in touch with you in order to sort this out. Best, Your RaceChip team

review_text: Hi there I bought the GTS model for my Vauxhall insignia 2.0 cdti 160hp I have it on the highest setting 7 I find it has made a difference to the car the extra torque has me driving around in sixth gear at around 36mph,so I have not noticed any more higher fuel consumption. I would also say that it drives a lot smoother as there's less lag, whether it's faster I would say it must be but not that you would notice unless you are booting it. Great support from the wholesalers if you buy direct , wait for an offer to come up on the website,I got £150 off the GTS model at Xmas.

Hi folks, I posted an average review for this product recently. However CS contacted me to offer support. My concern was the power increase was barely noticeable. Since then, well today actually, I drove my 2012XC90 for the first time since contacting CS. I’m not sure what, if anything they have done, but I now have a much more powerful car. I was quite shocked actually. Thanks Race Chip support 👍🏼

Good experience, tke kit seems to be working on my car, i feel a quicker acceleration especially on the second and third gear and this is exactly what I was looking for. Ordering, shipping and customer support was all fine and quick. So far all is good.

I bought the S version for my 2012 1.8 TSI Yeti and its done everything its said. Easy to install and easy to change the level of boost. I played around with the level of boost to see which was best suited. After a month I changed the boost level to 0 to see if my other half could tell the difference and sure enough after a day or so she complained the car didn't have the oomph off the lights as it did and could I look at it. So that's proof in its self. The beauty of adding these instead of a full remap is you can alter it as and when with no fuss. I'd recommend to anyone who is looking for a little more without spending big money.

Terrible tuning chip. I purchased one for my 2021 Ford Ranger directly from over sea’s that got to me rather quickly. Installation was pretty straight forward but it gave me absolutely no more power. There was no difference between stock and tune set to the performance setting. Basically an expensive paper weight. It was I nightmare to return and get reimbursed. Glad it’s behind me now.
supplier_response: Dear Nathan, thanks for your feedback. Engines have a different serial tolerance, this means that the performance given by the maker is not always the actual performance of the engine. Depending on the deviation (up or down) it can result in a different performance delta with tuning. For your engine, we have already used the maximum recommended setting. A further increase in the performance could cause a permanent overload, which is why we refrain from doing so. For the return you received an UPS return label. Best regards, Your RaceChip Team

Has caused major engine codes about every month or so, and the most recent one was a red code that slowed the car down to a halt. I was fortunate enough to pull into a driveway, disconnect it, and finally get to my destination.  Codes are gone after disconnecting.  From what I’ve seen the power gains were moderate, but the risk to my engine isn’t worth it.  Would not buy again.

review_text: Excellent Products.. Excellent Customer Services.. I Purchased The GTS And XLR Throttle Controller. I Experienced A Marked Improvement In Performance And I Am Very Pleased With My Purchases. Keep Up The Good Work.. Cheers. Russell.

So I bought a race chip s for my rather pedestrian fiesta 1.4 diesel, installation they said was a bit tricky, and yes it was but I got there, only one plug to plug into the fuel rail,but they sent me pictures of it, so big up to race chips, so I put it onto number 4 out of 5, and I could feel the difference straight away, better pick up, faster acceleration, 0 to 60 is two seconds up, and top end is 5 miles up, so for me money well spent, and I know ppl will say get a re map, no as its too much cash more than double, but not double the performance, and I phoned the tech team up, and they where very helpful,so a big thumbs up from me.

The RaceChip has made a big difference.  I was hesitant until I saw a tuning company I trust do dyno runs, as I've seen a lot of negativity suggesting the chips are not giving the power they claim. The install took longer than it should, as the instructions are both very poor in quality, and shockingly wrong.  I have a 2020 Alfa Romeo Giulia, and the connections are labelled the wrong way around! Luckily one is 3 pins and the other 4 pins, and I checked before trying to plug them in.  A lot of people will not check, and could damage the connections, in particular since the connection at the back of the engine is difficult to see, so done more by touch than sight.  You don't expect instructions or labels to be wrong! I'm unsure on the Bluetooth connection.  As there's no Apple/Android Carplay option, you have to unlock your phone and adjust it.  It means you end up leaving it in Race all the time, but if I was doing a long journey, I'd change to Eco. Decide to overtake on your journey, and you're in Eco, you're missing loads of power.  Adjust the setting on your phone mid journey and you're breaking the law.  It makes the option compromised, but better than having to pop the bonnet. If your car is under warranty, financed etc, then I'd go RaceChip.  If you're out of warranty and own the car, I'd go for a remap.  It's cheaper, and less compromised.

Ordered Racechip S for F55 (2017) Mini Cooper 1.5 Petrol. Right now, it's installed fine, taken for a test drive and the extra power is very noticeable! Overtakes are a lot easier and I'm more confident overtaking. I deducted 1 star for a few reasons: 1) The printed manual was for a BMW, which has an engine layout completely different to a Mini. 2) The RaceChip's connectors - which have an 'A' pipe and a 'B' pipe - were labelled the wrong way around. The 'A' pipe (supposedly for MAP Sensor) had 4 pins, whereas my Mini's MAP Sensor has 3; vice versa for the 'B' pipe (supposedly for Boost Sensor). The manual should be tailored to each individual car - like what BlueSpark does. However, RaceChip responded to my question (within 4 working days), with annotated photos of where the MAP and BP sensors are located on my Mini. They also explained the pipes could have been mislabelled. So, pretty good service. My one ride in my Mini with the RaceChip was excellent. The RaceChip S has 5 settings, defaulted to the 3rd map. I increased it to map 5, and the gains are huge - wouldn't want any more.

I have a race chip S installed on my 2006 R51 Pathfinder, its been on there since dec2020, and i couldn't be more pleased with it, it was easy to fit with clear instructions. I got the S as my pathfinder had done 165k miles and didn't want to destroy it, but needed a little more torque for towing as its my work truck, after a couple of weeks trying each tune for a few days i settled on number 4 and haven't looked back, its a night and day change, its gone from sluggish and boring to responsive and great fun and for £109 as opposed to £280 i was quoted for a remap. I did get an engine light come on but it was coincidence and completely unrelated to the chip, I've since added a K&N and 3'' straight pipe exhaust, after a few days of chip settling in again with no further changes to it the truck is so much fun and runs much more smoothly than it ever did stock, overtaking is fuss free and brisk and it always feels unstoppable with my work trailer on now. I cant comment on fuel economy as i have a lead foot, and the new found fun factor has not helped that. When i decided to buy it i went through these reviews a little sceptical of how well it would work, having now owned one and looked at them again it seams like most of the bad reviews have neither, read the instructions or spoken to technical support about their issues, their loss. The unit was delivered within three days so there is plenty of time to try it and ask about issue within the 30 days if you're not happy. Great work race chip, things that far exceed expectations for performance and service seam to be very rare these days, you make it look easy.

Absolutely LOVE this thing. Just showed up today, and WOW what a noticeable improvement in the lower gears. My A4 suddenly feels more like an S4. Can’t wait to get my hands on the XLR throttle tune as well, but for now I’m thoroughly impressed. If you’re looking for a great alternative to an ECU reflash, the RaceChip GTS is the way to go.

Ford Mondeo TitaniumX 07 2.5T, RS Chip. Had to remove the headlight for access and the RaceChip box now lives behind my fog lamp foam mounted in a waterproof vented container. Simple installation but hard to access. So tried it in race mode and my gas pedal is now called the whup ass pedal, well happy. My average mpg went down to 16mpg from 24mpg, no such thing as a free lunch! So before installing I put my car into cruise control at 60mph for 50 miles of motorway and got 33mpg. Repeated the experiment after installation. Same day, same route and with the chip set in “ECO” I got 41.8mpg?!!! I also had my wheel tracking done beforehand so don’t know how much difference that made but so far I’m well happy as even in “ECO” mode it’s faster.

After a few months on my brand new f40 118i m sport on start up my car went into limp mode as the racechip lost its power supply? I had to reset the box for the power light on the race chip to come back on and work I took of the race chip and advertised it for sale with no takers to date get a remap if you want reliability

review_text: Been running an RS box on my 1.5t Mini Cooper F57 for a few months now, and its great. Power is (as per Racechip figures) touching Cooper S levels, and whether thats accurate or not, it certainly feels like it. The only issue i had was that the labels on the connectors were wrong, but i'm mechanically minded and i realised the difference between the manifold and the turbo, so fitted correctly. Disappointed with brexit import charges, but thats not the companys fault, and their customer services helped solve a problem which had meant i'd paid more to import than i should have. Considering a GTS box for my 3 series diesel now...

True review about RaceChip S. Skoda Octavia mk2 - 1.9TDI Firstly-it came super quick, just as it says within 2 to 5 days. About the package-verry nicely packed and secured, only thing is that the chip itself was a bit dusty, but absolutley nothing to mind.. About the installation-instructions on the additional paper could be little better for my car specifficly but I mannaged to find the solution using YouTube. It is verry easy to do it yourself, just read everything first so you can understand it better and you are ready to go. Performace-power and torq-you can feel it instantly, expecially while takeovers and on freeway. Only downside is I can feel something like a little bump while going 160kmh+ and letting off my throthle. Don't know why but dont mind it. Fuel economy-there is a big chance that you won't feel any difference becuase you are going to push your car a lot now. At least in the first few weeks, but afterwards, there is no difference in fuel economy (at least for me). Would I recommend it? - YES.

Bought two chips for my Mercedes w177. From first day of installing product cars are going into the safe mode. Seller won't give refund. Their justification is that the 30 day deadline for refund has passed, which is correct but also is correct that they were warned about problems on cars from first day. I could understood that it was problems with one car but when it is with two cars that it is not by some accident. Also one of car needed to be replaced air flow sensor and they said to me that this is not problem that chip could cause. They did not give any solution for refund cost of replacing this sensor. Only solution is new software in chips. There is no any answer from  their side what if this is going to happening again. My advice is to not buy their product. This lesson is going to cost me around 950 euro. Don't be stupid as I was.
supplier_response: Dear Mr. Basic, thanks for your review. Since the RaceChip is an additional control unit it can only move within the ECU's tolerances. Therefore it can't damage any sensor in general. In this particular case: the RaceChip is not connected to the air flow sensor so it can't affect it. As we can see, our technical support had offered you a check and update of your RaceChip immediately. So if you would like to take this option please feel free to get back to us any time. Best regards Your RaceChip team

review_text: What a brilliant Pro product! I have had this on my BMW 320d for two years before installing it on my m135i for about a year now. (The change over was also free of charge if you have the GTS black) The power and torque has been unbelievable, you feel it straight away and also the fuel economy works well on eco (on the racechip) is better than stock fuel economy. A lot of work/research/testing has been done by racechip to get the software working well (I also follow them on YouTube where they take you through the development) and the power difference whenever I need it has been fantastic. When you buy the chip, get the app on your phone because then you can switch maps effortlessly between eco, sport and race. Great work guys!

review_text: Absolutely astonished by the difference in power and fuel economy. Honestly couldn’t be happier. Feels like a completely different car and knocked off 2.1 seconds 0-60 😂👌😁

Bought a racechip S for my Pajero Sport 2.4D last December 03,2020.Delivered to my place in Philippines (Southeast Asia) after 6 days which early than I expected due to pandemic. It was well packed, complete manuals, and even sent me the picture (same w/ my unit) if where to connect. It's so easy to install without encountering any errors or CEL. I started on setting 3 (default), observed no rough idle, then test drive.. I felt immediately the improvement in acceleration. Next tried setting 4 ...Wow!! the acceleration was more strong and smooth. I could not believed it how it behave in acceleration without any hesitation or delay ha,ha,ha...Then I switched On also my existing throttle controller (other brand)..It's become more fun to drive.Very satisfied even with S variant as I wanted only to improve more the acceleration of my SUV. The Racechip customer service is great based on my experienced with them. It's already more than a month of use.. and luckily no CEL or problems encountered so far...Very good chip for the price!!

I was very sceptical about a 'tuning box' for £109 ( 'S' version, cheapest one for my car at time of this review) but I am pleasantly surprised , my vehicle is a jaguar x type 2.2 diesel with 190k on the clock and with this fitted is now much faster ,smoother and much more enjoyable to drive, it came packaged well and was easy to install, very happy to transform the performance for such little money.

Recently bought the RaceChip Rs with app control. Installing was super easy, probably took around 5 minutes. I let the car idle for a few minutes to make sure nothing was wrong, then took it out for a quick drive to see if I noticed a difference. I cycled through Eco, sport, and race. There was a noticeable difference between the 3 and a difference between the "stock tune" and race tune. Of course I was just doing an old fashioned butt dyno but the car felt like it had more on tap then it used to. For the RS with the Bluetooth connection it was 379usd (they were running a Christmas sale). All in all so far I am super pleased with it and have no complaints. Customer service was great and shipping was fairly quick seeing as how I'm in Alaska and it was shipped from Germany.

I purchased this chip in the black Friday offer, like most I had my doubts about the company and product due to it all seeming a little to easy to get such power gains. If I was to take my car to a dyno for a tune it was going to take it from 185bhp to 217bhp which I was really excited about doing. However, when I saw that the chip was going to offer a gain from 185bhp to 240bhp I had to investigate. Due to the chip being on offer making more sense for me to spend the money and the company offering a 30 day return period I decided to give it a go. The product arrived in 4 days which was great as I live in UK and it was shipped from Germany. The product install was done in 10-15 mins due to the personal install package they send you via email. So far been driving with it for a few days and it was worth every penny, the car can now bearly put its power down in second without spinning its absolutely fantastic. As a student, it really was a risk spending so much money but going fast is my passion so I don't have any regrets when it comes to the chip. Hope this helps someone in the same position as I was about a tuning box. UPDATE - Used product for 4 years with no issues and been happy with the product since day 1, 4 years later i have bought a new car and i messaged racechip to get the chip reprogrammed only to find out they only support this for up to 24 months after purchase. Although this was mentioned in the T&C's it was not made clear at the time of purchase and has left me disappointed. Even if they offered a service where you can pay to get the chip changed at a reduced price to buying another as a show that they care about long term customers would be nice.

Well, I wasn't sure about chip tuning… like… I really wasn’t sure. I had just bought my dream car – one that wasn’t killing the environment, but also had a bit of poke and gets me up and down the mountain that I live up in Austria – even in snow and ice.  (It’s a UK registered Jaguar XF 20 AWD with 180 ps and 430 nm). So, its a proper nice car, but not that pokey (acceleration) as I had been driving a Skoda VRS before, and that goes as fast as Donald J Trump after a cheeseburger, so, naturally after a while I began to think I really should have got the Jaguar 25 AWD with 241ps). It was then that I understood that essentially the two cars are identical (suspension, brakes, interior, etc.) with the exception that the ‘more powerful’ and much more expensive 25 AWD is just faster because of the twin turbo, so. Suddenly, I worked out, I might be able to get 25 AWD performance for a few hundred Euros, rather than several thousand it would get to buy the 25 AWD which are about 20% more expensive on the second hand market. So, I asked a mate of mine who drives ridiculous German cars: S6, AMG Jeep type thing – utterly bonkers. He doesn’t talk much normally (he just likes his cars), and his reaction was weird. For the first time in a lifetime he just wouldn’t shut up about how ‘effing brilliant chip tuning was. Well, that avalanche of praise from an otherwise ‘quiet man’ convinced me and the next day, I took the plunge and ordered the smallest chip (the S) to test it out and see what it might do. It arrived a couple of days later. The wife was curious (she always gets to the post first) and I told her it was a thing to save fuel. She was totally suspicious “Why doesn’t everyone have one then?” she asked. “Round here?” I countered looking up and down the valley. We live surrounded by mountain farmers who drive tractors by day and big Audis by night. “I expect most already do… Its only 169 Euros” I said. “I’ll order one for you tomorrow, just give me the cash.” I could see her weighing up how much cat food she could buy for that much money, and to be honest, it wasn’t even a mildly fair contest. Within seconds she was back to annimal videos on her phone.  Job done. With that now taken care of, it was time to get it installed. Well, I’m an academic by trade, so more of a philospohy type, than a spanner and wrench one; not really very ‘hands on’, but also not stupid. Anyway, it took me about 10 minutes to get it all wired up, they give you a whole bunch of instructions (with pictures), that make IKEA building look difficult, so its really a nice piece of customer service. With this done, I then took the Jag out for a test drive, and the difference was noticeable. I had been missing that little kick in the small of the back when accelerating (yes, sad but true, I have been missing the little VRS – who would believe it?), and now, it seemed like the Jag had suddenly gone from a nice looker, to a ‘nearly’ exciting performer.  I drove up and down the mountain once on the winding serpentine roads; night time, all to myself, and sure enough, found myself grinning like a school boy. There you go compatriots, that is what you need. That is the real test, whether it makes you smile or not, and it did… but, not quite enough. I realised I needed the bigger chip, the GTS. (Naturally, there is a whole marketing strategy behind the chip tuning industry, and I am now in the thick of it). Well, there you go, that’s my story. In my opinion, the thing to look out for (especially in a diesel like my Jag XF and it’ll be the same in a 5 series or an A6, or an E class) is how much the torque increases - not so much the Horse Power.: although to be fair, they say the ps has gone from 180 to 214 PS, so that's not bad either What you are looking at is a signficant power gain further down the rev spectrum, say mid- 2k for nm: as well as a noticiable one than over 5k for bp. So, this means when your mates down the pub (Kneipe for my German friends; Wirtshaus where I live), ask you (as they will) 'Wieviel PS alter?", and with the GTS chip (the big brother) you have to talk about the stonking, beautiful, galvansing 540 nm you have (and possibly leave out the 230 ps). Thing is, you don't get to honestly say “380 ps alter”, which is what the big V6 3.0 Diesel Jaguar has with EXACTLY THE SAME amount of Newtons as the GTS chip would give my modest cat!!! At the moment my RaceChip ‘S’ tuned Jag has 503 NM with a chip that cost me 160 Euros, and if I do eventually decide to get the GTS chip, and drive around with 540 Newtownians, I may not have the nervy-edgy racy feel of 380 horses, but I will have the firm, powerful push with more NM than the brand new ‘BMW 540’, with only 500 nm. I will have 5 more nm than the legendary 2020 Porsche Carrera 4S, for considerably less, and that is probably ‘it’ in a nutshell. "More for less". There, put that in your pipe and smoke it.

Racechip GTS installed on a Skoda Kodiaq 2.0TSI 'CZPA' engine. From order to delivery the process was slick and fast given the package was shipped halfway round the world. Customer services were responsive when I requested more pictures of the sensor placement and the installation instructions supplied in the box were very clear. The install was trickier than expected, largely due to the boost pressure sensor being really only accessible from under the car and the Kodiaq undertray (unlike a Golf or Audi A3) is secured on by many more bolts aswell as screws. I was only able to do this because I had the car up on ramps. Apart from access to the boost pressure sensor, the actual installation of the harness and set-up of the Racechip unit was fantastically simple. Must admit to being initially disappointed by the performance gain, even on Race7. I would best describe it as 'mild'. HOWEVER, I soon realised that this was likely due to the frankly awful stock throttle pedal calibration of the Kodiaq - inconsistent with a dead spot for the first ~20% of pedal travel. Installed a cheap throttle pedal controller which has dramatically improved the responsiveness of the car and you can now fully exploit the power gains from the Racechip GTS to the extent that I have now had to wind the Racechip back to Sport6. My advice to anyone considering a Racechip GTS for a 2.0TSI 'CZPA' engine in a Kodiaq or Tiguan is do it...BUT budget for the Racechip XLR too.

review_text: Just excellent, there are all kinds of opinions around the web. But most of the negative ones are of car programmers. So I gave it a chance and I couldn't be happier. It comes setted with map 3, and I couldn't notice any difference, changed to 4 and there it was! I tried 5, and it was faster, but with some jumps so I went back to 4 to have a more continuous response.

Absolutely avoid this product!! I'd like to address a few issues with this product which have also been highlighted by others. I Bought the GTS model, upon arrival it came with generic instructions, whilst I appreciate those who are absolute car enthusiast may know where to find the turbo pressure sensor and Map sensor, for the average person just wanting to do a little extra to there car this isnt as straight forward. You have to email them to obtain instructions specifically for your vehicle and from reading their FAQ this is clearly a problem that many consumers have had and never actually been addressed. When you're paying £300 + for a product I'd expect some instructions. After joining other Facebook forums I managed to obtain instructions from other sources as racechip took so long to reply I managed to get it fitted. Upon initially driving the car you can notice the difference almost immediately, clear power and torque increase and loved it. All to good to be true after about a week I began to notice my rev counter appeared to be slipping whilst the chip was on and happened regardless of what mode it was in (race, sport, eco). Approximately 1 week after this my car began judder and was hesitant when putting my foot down and again revs kept slipping. I made contact with racechip and they advised that they would send a new update to my chip, this process was quick to install but the problems I've mentioned above became even more apparent. This Monday I decided I want to nip to shop and get some stuff, not long after I left the house I noticed the issues again and began to smell oil coming through my air vents and smoke from the engine bay. When I stopped and lifted the bonnet it looked like there had been and explosion of oil, immediately began to think I blew a head gasket or done some damage to the engine. Later took it into the garage and it turned out to just be a cylinder head cap and seal that had come off and shot oil all over the side of the engine. I didn't initially think it was anything to do with the racechip and but it down to just wear and tear of the engine and my luck really. Managed to get this replaced and decided to turn off the chip for a while because of the hot weather and possibly causing any more damage to the engine. Since doing that the car ran really smooth again and had absolutely know issues up until I decided to turn the chip back on today and put it into eco mode. I took about a 10 min drive to my local asda and on the way back began to notice similar issues that I mentioned at the start again, about 500m from my house loss power again and smell of oil began to fill the air vents again. Due to what previously happened I decided to check the same area where the original repairs were made and immediately noticed the 2nd cylinder head cap and seal had come off and shot oil all over the engine again. Tomorrow I intend on completely removing the chip from my car and returning it back to how it was, I can't obviously say that the issues I've had have all been down to the chip but this is the only variable I have changed on the car and only noticed them whilst the chip is active. It appears that there is just too much pressure and stress being put on the engine and Im gonna try and prevent anything further happening to my car. I wish I had listened to the other reviews people had said about tuning chips and in particularly racechip but I gave them the benefit of the doubt and became a foolish consumer of the product. This is my warning to all those out there who want to make changes to your car, do not buy this product, get your car remapped professionally if you intend to do anything. From reading other recent reviews I have seen that people just end up getting into a back and forth war with racechip about the faults with this product and there reluctance to help. With that I am just going to learn my lesson, cut my losses and never purchase another tuning chip.

review_text: I fitted a Racechip RS to my T5.1 today straight out the box, followed instructions 20 minutes later all good. Performance has far exceeded my expectations and it is running like a dream. Great product and worth every penny.

Great performance and quality! I installed the RS unit, Harness, and chip in less than 20 minutes and mounted it carefully next to my normal ECU, the only minor set back that occurred was figuring out where and what the Bluetooth password was, (which is the last 6 digits of the serial number on the unit)  but after that the system booted up properly and it began working quite quickly, taking full effect in about 1.5 - 2 hours. I started out using it on level 3 of [Sport Mode] which by itself made made a huge difference in low end torque and boost, along with a increase in rev range, Later that evening my wife wanted to feel it in “Race Mode” which I agreed to, and switched over the preset, and Oh. My. God. Did it kick my car into high gear, I drive a pretty Quick and well modified performance car as it is, but this was unlike anything I’ve experienced as far as the nature of the car, the acceleration: Brutal. The rev- Range: High, The torque: Head rest smacking. What more is there to say?? Final thoughts: I went into this extremely skeptical, I had seen a lot of conflicting reviews and misinformation about this product and company, along with a lot of paid sponsorships, so I was more than a little Leary at first, but upon installing it in the correct manner and using some common sense, I now love my car even more then I did before.

Best money ever spent on trying to improve an I30

I installed it last week and I am very impressed.  Thank goodness for traction control.  If tuned off the tires break loose anywhere under 20 mph. Since I will keep it in race mode which has little effect unless you push it, I don't really need the bluetooth feature.

Throttle response is excellent I have a gts black box And I invested the extra 50 GBP For the Bluetooth app as I previously had a blue spark in my old bmw and I had to keep popping the hood to change maps.(which was very annoying) I bought the tuning box mainly for the higher output map and when I’m not on the higher map I just put it into eco. I bought the cheapest RaceChip for my SEAT Leon Fr and keeping it on the middle 3 setting I was getting better MPG and better performance.  But after about a month, the car would occasionally hiccup and on one occasion, on the motorway, a dashboard warning came on and the car went into limp mode.  When I got home, I turned off the engine, turned it back on again and it was running fine – no warning lights. So I knocked the setting down to 2 and then 1 and even though it gave me miles of OK driving, it would still hiccup occasionally.  During this time I was emailing customer service who have been absolutely superb throughout.  Then, on setting 1, it started going into limp mode almost continually and even did so again on the motorway, so, on the motorway hard shoulder I turned it to 0 to get back OK. I then contacted customer service who suggested I return it for a re-program.  They supplied the return postage label and I got it back a week later.  Unfortunately, I then got worse MPG on all of the settings.  So I contacted customer service again, just to advise them of the history of operation – I did not request or expect a refund – in my mind I had written the cost off to experience.  However, completely unprompted, they said if I returned it they would give me a full refund.  They again sent a label and issued the refund within a week. That is why I give 4 stars – because their customer service has been superb – just a shame that the chip didn’t work perfectly with my car.

Brilliant. It's given my throttle the extra punch it needed. Fitted this to a 2001 BMW 330Ci (E46). It's electronic throttle and I've always found it a little laggy. I was sceptical about fitting the RaceChip unit but I'm glad I took the risk. Installation was easy (although the sticky pads are not sticky at all), and the unit and accessories are well made and solid. Performance has been great. Genuinely, the rev range and layout feels better, particularly in the higher settings. I'm a real E46 nerd, and can honestly say that this unit has added great responsiveness to the throttle. S and S+ mode are good for daily driving. R and R+ mode aren't comfortable when in start/stop traffic, but on a clear and open road it's fantastic. This installation has been a nice surprise. It's important to understand that this doesn't add power, or a remap, but it does adjust the sensitivity of your throttle, more so than just planting your foot could ever manage. It puts down the power a lot quicker . Ultimately, it's a sport button for your car. Would definitely recommend.

review_text: Ich bin vor mittlerweile mehr als einem halben Jahr über Instagram auf diese Firma aufmerksam geworden und habe mir probehalber ein paar ihrer Produkte bestellt, seitdem bestelle ich regelmäßig nach. Die verschiedenen Reiniger sind ebenso qualitativ hochwertig wie innovativ (säurefrei, umweltschonend) und kommen von einem Unternehmen, dessen Gründer mit Herzblut dabei sind, die Pakete mitunter selbst packen und verschicken und sich auf ihren Kanälen redlich Mühe geben eine möglichst persönliche und unmittelbare Kundenbetreuung zu bieten. Ich erwähne die Verlosungen bewusst zuletzt, weil ich auch ohne die Loschance auf einen sonst nur zu erträumende Fahrzeuge diese Produkte kaufen und weiterempfehlen würde. Dass man pro bezahltem Euro auf zuerst einen auf 333 Stück limitierten A1 Quattro, dann auf einen auf 999 Stück limitierten und getunten Audi R8 V10 RWD, dann auf ein Zweijahresleasing eines Golf 8GTI TCR und nun auf einen Porsche 991.1 GT3RS auf Lebenszeit mit Übernahme sämtlicher Kosten (außer Sprit) für ein Jahr erhält, ist die wohl saftigste Kirsche auf der Sahnehaube, die es gegenwärtig irgendwo gibt, und es unterstreicht für mich einfach mit jeder Live-Verlosung, mit wieviel Leidenschaft Viamontis dabei ist und, weswegen es sich immer lohnt aufstrebende Unternehmen für ihren Mut und Innovationsgeist zu unterstützen! Wer bis hier mitgelesen hat, der/dem danke ich für die Aufmerksamkeit, und wer diesen Beitrag nur überflogen hat, der/dem gebe ich mit: es gab nie bessere Gründe das eigene Zwei-,Drei- oder Vierrad zu pflegen, als mit den erstklassigen Produkten von Viamontis. Überzeugt euch selbst! I became aware of this company more than half a year ago via Instagram and ordered a few of their products on a trial basis, since then I regularly reorder. The various cleaners are as high quality as they are innovative (acid-free, environmentally friendly) and come from a company whose founders put their heart and soul into it, sometimes packing and shipping the packages themselves and making every effort to offer the most personal and direct customer service possible on their social channels. I deliberately mention the raffles last because I would buy and recommend these products even without the chance of winning a vehicle that I could otherwise only dream of. That they give one ticket per paid euro towards first winning a limited to 333 units A1 Quattro, then towards a limited to 999 units and tuned Audi R8 V10 RWD, then towards a two-year leasing of a Golf 8GTI TCR and now towards a Porsche 991. 1 GT3RS for life with all costs paid (except fuel) for one year is probably the juiciest cherry on top of the cream that is currently available anywhere, and for me it simply underlines with every raffle with how much passion Viamontis is involved and why it is always worth supporting up-and-coming companies for their courage and innovative spirit! For those of you who have been reading along up to this point, thank you for your attention, and for those of you who have only skimmed throughy this article, I can tell you that there have never been better reasons to maintain your own two, three or four-wheeler than with the first-class products from Viamontis. Treat yourselves!
supplier_response: Hallo Jan, deine Bewertung war die ist die wohl saftigste Kirsche auf der Sahnehaube, was Bewertungen angeht, die wir bislang bekommen haben. Wir sagen DANKE für diesen einzigartigen Support und deine objektiven Worte. Wir geben jeden einzelnen Tag unser absolut Bestes, um noch mehr Menschen von uns und unseren Visionen zu überzeugen. (In manchen Fällen leider heutzutage gar nicht so einfach). Ebenso arbeiten wir laufend daran noch transparenter zu werden (obwohl wir da vermutlich eh schon Benchmark in diesem Bereich sind). Nochmal tausend Dank für deine Bewertung. Wir drücken dir ganz fest die Daumen für die Auslosungen. Viele liebe Grüße. Das Viamontis Team

I am writing this to warn other drivers, especially those in the Nuremberg/Erlangen area. I ordered 4 summer tires for my car and selected their "official" mounting partner, Ilka Automobile (Fuggerstr. 29, 90439 Nuremberg), during the checkout process. ​After the tires were dispatched, I personally drove to the address to coordinate the appointment, only to find a residential apartment building. There is no workshop, no signage, and no professional tire service at this location. It is a ghost address. ​When I contacted customer support, their response was shocking. They admitted they "no longer offer mounting stations" in that way, yet they still actively list them as verified partners on their website. Worse, they told me it was my responsibility to "personally contact" the workshop before ordering-even though their own system presents these shops as ready-to-use partners. ​The Reality: ​Misleading Information: They are taking money for a service (delivery to a partner) that does not exist. ​Poor Support: Instead of taking responsibility for their outdated database, they blamed me for not calling a "partner" they officially recommended. ​Logistical Nightmare: My expensive tires are now in transit to a residential building where they cannot be fitted, risking loss or theft. ​If you are in need of wheels that require professional mounting, avoid their partner list. They are misleading customers with a database that is clearly not maintained.

I replied that they should simply charge my card — that’s why I provided my card details. Since there was no reaction, I finally transferred the money manually via online banking as well. A week later, I got an email saying the tires would soon be handed over to a courier. A few days later, the courier arrived — but only brought two tires and had no idea where the other two were. He said they would probably come a few days later. No further email arrived, but a few days later I found the other two tires just lying on the street in front of my house, without any packaging. The courier didn’t ring the bell or ask for a signature, although the shop had explicitly written “delivery against signature”. In the end, the tires did arrive — but only after three weeks, even though the website said “in stock, delivery in 3–4 days.” Not one star only because the tires finally arrived.

The refund was the wrong one for 3 instead of just 1 tyre and even then no refund was made. Eventually I was notified that the one remaining tyre was being delivered and eventually it arrived. In conclusion the company relies on different suppliers and different delivery services and when it goes wrong it is hard to communicate to the right team directly so that the customer is given reassurance about the status on the order process. I suggest that a better direct means of communication is provided to avoid such issues. Unfortunately this process has made myself not consider this company in future due to its unreliability and loss of confidence

This is my review following my installation of two rear, complete strut assemblies for my 2013 Cayenne Diesel (with standard suspension). The reason I am giving these struts only 2 stars is because although the parts looked like decent quality when they arrived, (a) they were extremely difficult to install, and (b) the rear ride height is now higher by about 2.5 inches than the front. I believe the Aerosus replica strut assemblies are longer than the OEMs but, I cannot be absolutely sure because I did not measure them against the OEMs I removed.   Why?   Because both of the rear springs on the OEMs had broken so any measurement would not have been accurate. However, if I could post pictures on this review, you - the reader  - can judge for yourself WHETHER the rear ride height looks normal.  With the OEMs, there was no differential ... I believe ... and even if there was, it was not noticeable to the naked eye. Look, maybe the Aerosus replicas will "settle down"  as the company claims.  If it does, then, I will retract this review and post a new one.  For now, this review is accurate

I am very disappointed with my recent experience with Autodoc.I placed an order for Pirelli tires on 27.02.2026 and received them on 11.03.2026. However, I later discovered that the tires have DOT codes from 01/2023 and 02/2023. This means the tires were already over 3 years old at the time of delivery, which is not what I expect when purchasing a “new” product in 2026.Since then, I have been dealing with this issue for almost a month. During this time, I have not been able to complete a necessary tire change, which has affected my ability to use my vehicle safely.In addition, I have had to store, move, and handle four tires multiple times due to this situation, which caused unnecessary physical effort and inconvenience — all because of incorrect or misleading expectations regarding the product.The most frustrating part is the lack of a satisfactory solution. I requested a reasonable compensation, considering the age of the tires and the inconvenience caused. Instead, I received only a minimal offer and repeated delays.I am based in Switzerland, and returning the tires is not simple or cost-effective. Despite this, I was informed that I may need to handle the return logistics myself, which I find unacceptable given that the issue is not caused by me.For a company of this size, I expected a much more customer-oriented approach and a fair resolution.If this matter is not resolved properly, I will consider taking further steps through consumer protection channels.I sincerely hope Autodoc will take this complaint seriously and provide a fair and reasonable solution.

review_text: I ordered a SACHS flywheel (2294 501 267) from Autodoc, paying a premium SACHS price.What I received was a broken, recycled LUK flywheel, inside a SACHS box, tied together with zip ties and taped shut. The flywheel had huge play throughout, making it completely unsafe for installation.SACHS/ZF confirmed that this flywheel is not even produced by SACHS, but sourced from LUK for rare VWAG models. Yet Autodoc never disclosed this anywhere, selling it as SACHS at a premium price.The price difference is shocking: in Bulgaria it can be €350–€450, while on other European sites it is only about €150, yet the product inside is identical to a much cheaper LUK part. Autodoc profits massively by misleading customers.This is misleading, unsafe, and completely unacceptable. I returned the part the same day, but Autodoc failed to resolve the issue, leaving my car unusable for 2 months and causing 4 months of delays, frustration, and extra costs.Autodoc must stop misleading customers and clearly disclose when parts are sourced from third parties, especially when they are broken or unsafe.

review_text: Very disappointing and misleading experience with AutodocMy experience with Autodoc has been extremely frustrating and disappointing.I ordered spare parts after Autodoc’s website explicitly confirmed compatibility with my vehicle. My VIN number is already saved in my personal account, and based on this information, the website assured that the parts were suitable. However, when the parts arrived, they turned out to be completely incompatible.As a result, I had to return the items and paid shipping costs twice (to and from Geneva), totaling approximately CHF 85. Autodoc refunded only the price of the parts and refused to reimburse the shipping costs, even though the mistake was entirely theirs.Instead of taking responsibility, they attempted to blame the customer by claiming that selecting parts by make and model is “not accurate.” This raises a serious question: why does their website confirm compatibility if it is unreliable?This was not my first bad experience with Autodoc. Previously, I was offered a compensation voucher for a similar mistake, which later turned out to be invalid and unusable. Now they repeat the same approach by offering a small discount coupon instead of refunding the actual costs caused by their error.In summary:Incorrect and incompatible partsCustomer forced to pay for the company’s mistakesUnreliable vouchersAvoidance instead of real solutionsA very poor customer experience. I will not use Autodoc again and cannot recommend them.
supplier_response: Hello Sabah Jassem! We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience and frustration you’ve experienced. Please be aware that the parts displayed on our website whether selected through the vehicle selector or by entering your registration number are intended as general recommendations. Because vehicles often have unique specifications beyond just the model and body type, the most accurate way to confirm compatibility is by using the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) or the Original Equipment Number (OEN). Even if your VIN is stored in your account, our system does not automatically verify compatibility against it. This important step must be carried out by our trained specialists to ensure the correct fit. Our customer support team is always available to help with a full compatibility check, as product listings only provide technical details and cannot guarantee suitability for every vehicle. Please rest assured that our Quality Control Manager will be reaching out to you shortly to personally review your case and provide further assistance, ensuring the matter is handled properly. Best regards, AUTODOC Team

review_text: I ordered a steering rack for my 2009 Audi A4 B8 2.0l TDI (143hp) 2 weeks ago. The delivery was fast, it arrived in only a few days, which i liked. Yet it turns out a part was missing in the delivery: The metal plug. Instead, it was delivered with a plastic one to keep the dust from entering. According to my local mechanic, without the right plug / lock, the plastic one wouldn't keep up with the oil pressure and it would just explode.I have tried to contact AUTODOC in multiple ways.-The AI assistant on their app told me I'd get an e-mail in 24-48 hours, 4 days later I haven't received anything.-I have called their numbers in hope of reaching an actual human instead of an AI, but guess what. Dan the virtual assistant picked up and he was no help at all. I could repeat a sentence 3 times and he wouldn't understand a thing I said, so after some time he gave up and said "We're happy we could solve your problem!"Next I wanted to see if it's possible to atleast return the steering rack, but no, "Unfortunately, this product is not eligible for a refund."I spent a total of 480 bucks on this thing, and for someone at the age of 19, I simply cannot afford this waste of money.And even if this so called "plug" isn't actually included in the product, then at least help me find the missing piece I need.I might not be experienced in cars and I could also be wrong about what I said in the beginning, it might just be called something else or it might just be an entirely other piece that I'm talking about. My main point is that there is literally no way for me to reach out to AUTODOC because of their awfully designed AI assistant.
supplier_response: Hello ! We’re very sorry to read about your experience and understand how frustrating this situation must be, especially given the importance and cost of the part. Regarding your case, we would like to clarify that we have attempted to contact you, however the phone number and email address provided with the order appear to be invalid, which prevents our team from reaching you directly. To properly investigate the missing metal plug, check the product specifications, and offer you the correct solution (replacement part, clarification, or return options), we kindly ask you to contact us directly by email at trust@autodoc.de. Please include clear photos of the received steering rack, and the area where the plug should be installed. Once we receive your email, our support team will review the case manually and assist you as quickly as possible. We truly regret the inconvenience and appreciate your patience. Best regards, AUTODOC Team

review_text: After posting this complaint, I was eventually contacted and reimbursed for the incompatible parts. However, after a few messages, the employee who had initially reached out to me appeared to stop responding, which forced me to contact the in-app support again. Only then was a warranty claim filed and my money refunded. While I am grateful for the resolution, I remain concerned about the way it was handled.The company referred to this outcome as a ‘gesture of goodwill.’ In reality, complying with consumer protection law is not goodwill—it is a legal obligation. What troubles me most is that, instead of straightforward assistance, I personally had to spend a great deal of time researching laws, studying specific legal articles, and presenting them to prove that I had the right to a refund.I appreciate the final resolution, but the process was unnecessarily time-consuming, frustrating, and placed the entire burden on me as the customer.Order number: 119912765Order date: 10.09.2024I am extremely disappointed with Autodoc’s customer service and their refusal to take responsibility for an incorrect part selection.All my previous orders for my Honda Accord 8 (VIN: JHMCU35809C203590) were always placed through Autodoc’s support team, never by myself. I always relied on their staff to provide the correct parts. However, in this case Autodoc now falsely claims that I ordered the parts on my own without their involvement, which is absolutely not true.The lower control arms that I received do not fit my vehicle. This is a clear case of “Sachmangel” under §434 BGB (German Civil Code) — the goods do not conform to the contract, as they are not suitable for the intended purpose. According to §439 BGB, in such cases the seller is obliged to provide a correct replacement or a full refund, and also to compensate the customer for costs of removal/installation.Instead, Autodoc is trying to hide behind a 14-day return period, which is irrelevant here. The 14-day return policy only applies to voluntary returns. When the goods are not as described or do not match the contract due to the seller’s mistake, the time limit does not apply — this is confirmed by EU consumer law (Directive 1999/44/EC and Directive (EU) 2019/771 on consumer sales and guarantees).In other words:•	The parts were selected incorrectly by Autodoc staff (as in all my previous orders).•	The parts do not fit — this is legally a non-conforming good.•	Autodoc must provide a replacement or refund under BGB §§434–439 and EU Directive 2019/771.•	Refusing support and shifting blame onto the customer is a breach of EU consumer rights.I am now forced to escalate this case to the European Consumer Centre (ECC-Net) and file a formal complaint. This whole experience has shown me that Autodoc’s customer support is unwilling to take responsibility when their own mistake causes problems for the buyer.⚠️ Buyers beware: if Autodoc makes a mistake in selecting your parts, they will try to deny responsibility and hide behind irrelevant “return policies.”
supplier_response: Hello Александр Пятковский! We regret you faced all the inconvenience. Our Quality Control Manager will be contacting you shortly to review your case and assist you further. Best regards, AUTODOC Team

review_text: I ordered some parts from AUTODOC and when they arrived in the UK at the EVRI parcel delivery depo, the EVRI tracking system told me “This parcel is bigger than we expected, so a specialist Evri courier will need to deliver it.”So it is coming up to 5 days that the parcel has been with EVRI, and I am still waiting to hear when my parcel is going to be delivered.I contacted AUTODOC told them the parcel was oversized.   AUTODOC said “It is very unlikely that the package was oversized. All parts are inside normal package 750x200x950”.I have confirmed with EVRI and their size limit is “Add together the 2 shortest sides and multiply it by 2. Then add the length. If the total is less than 245cm, your good to go”.So doing this with the dimensions AUTODOC gave me for my parcel (750x200x950) the calculation would be 200 +  750 = 950.   Then 950 x 2 = 1900.Then take the 1900 + 950 = 2850!   A total of 2850mm shows this parcel is over the EVRI size limit of 2450mm.So it is oversized for EVRI based on AUTODOC’s own admissions.EVRI also tells parcel senders “If your parcel is Overweight or Oversized then we’ll send the additional costs on to the sender and keep the parcel until we receive payment”.So if AUTODOC don’t admit what they have done and look into what I have told them (will AUTODOC do this, because as far as AUTODOC are concerned the delivery is still not classified as late or there isn’t a size issue as far as they are concerned) so looking at other complaints on Trustpilot this could be weeks before this is sorted out.I have to also add this is the Second order in a row now, I have had a delivery issue with.So I have 4 direct questions for AUTODOC which are as follows.1)	Why do you send out oversized parcels to EVRI?2)	Even if this was an AUTODOC accident sending it via EVRI, why does you customer service team not know about the size limit with EVRI and go immediately to resolve the problem?3)	Is the issue I have having also happening to others?4)	When am I going to get my parcel?AUTODOC if you reply to this post, please give actual direct answers to all my questions and not some standard holding comment like “Your case has been referred to the quality control department and will be considered as soon as possible.”Thank you.John
supplier_response: Hello John, We are sorry you faced inconveniences. We will check situation with the parcels' sizes. Our quality control manager will contact you in the nearest time. Best Regards, AUTODOC Team

Few months ago I purchased a product on eBay from ATP Autotelie, now it broke because of a clear defect (it broke in two parts), and due to its breakage I was close to get my car engine completely burned. I had to spend more money to replace the defective product on an emergency basis, with a lot of time waste.Not even three months were passed, so the product was and still is under purchase warranty coverage, which is defined by the UE Council directive 85/374/CEE of 25th July 1985.However, ATP Autotelie has blocked all ways to contact them or rise any kind of issue.Therefore, I tried try to assert my customer rights through the PayPal claiming system, but the seller invented the excuse that somehow I “altered” the product, which is clearly false and can be easily verified from the picture I sent them. Anyway, PayPal decided to support the fraud and rejected my claim.The matter does not end here, I am reporting what happened (all of which can be proven with documentation in hand) first here on TrustPilot, and then I am turning to a consumer defense association to take legal action, not only against the seller but also against PayPal.This is not so much for an economic problem, but because people cannot be defrauded in this way, it is a question of principle and a question of law, both national and European community laws.**** Update ****After the review was published on TrustPilot, I was contacted by ATP Autoteile, unlocking the possibility to message them on eBay messaging system (but why it was blocked, nobody said).They behaved like they didn't know anything about the claim, that looks quite suspicious to me: did eBay arbitrarily take the initiative to reject my complaint without even informing the seller and without any reasoning? Let's take this as the truth, since the level of eBay service is so poor that can actually arrive at this point.After this, they formally apologized (formally) and accepted to refund the faulty product (except shipping costs), without wanting the broken product back. Then. we had days and days of endless email exchange to undergo the steps of the refund process, several their emails were also sent me twice from different email address. If I could count all the time I lost to reply and send all the information they asked, probably I had to receive three-four times the due amount, but probably this was exactly the idea under such behavior.Obviously I just received the refund of the faulty product (except shipping costs), that is already a huge step on towards the right direction, but the experience was so frustrating that I cannot avoid helping others to avoid my same mistake.

review_text: I’m pretty sure that this review makes no difference to ATP or my case, but hopefully people will think twice before buying anything from this company.I purchased a Sachs clutch kit from ATP, for my Audi A4. The payment and delivery went fine and quick, which is probably the only positive thing I have to say about this company.We had scheduled a repair at a local mechanic for a gearbox and clutch replacement, so we delivered the ATP clutch as per agreement to the mechanic. However, when the mechanic went to fit the new clutch to the car, he noticed that the clutch didn’t fit and was actually a LUK clutch (completely different brand to Sachs). The clutch was branded LUK on one side and Sachs on the other.As the car was taking up space on a lift and the mechanic couldn’t wait for a new clutch to be delivered, we had to buy the correct clutch locally. Unfortunately it didn’t come with a clutch release bearing, so we had to use the one supplied with the clutch kit from ATP.I called ATP and explained the situation (in German, as apparently only one or two ATP employees speaks English) and asked if it was possible for me to return the incorrect clutch without the bearing, to which they replied yes.I returned the clutch as agreed, and for a long period of time I heard nothing from them, so I decided to call them to see if they received the clutch. After a couple of calls, they informed me that they had in fact received the clutch, but that the bearing was missing and that they could not refund me as the set was not complete. I tried to explain the situation several times with no luck and no sympathy.ATP sells the exact clutch release bearing on their website and I informed them, that I would happily pay for the bearing that I had used from the kit, so they could replace it in the kit. But for some reason this is impossible to do for ATP. In theory I could just get the clutch back, buy the bearing, put it in the box and return a complete set.I have now spent several hours on the phone, trying to first of all get through to them on the phone, which is a nightmare. And when I finally manage to get through, nobody speaks English (fortunately I speak a little German). The employees that answer the phone cannot make any decisions and needs to speak to their supervisors and promises to call back, which they NEVER do, so you have to start all over every time you get through to them.To make things even better, now ATP wants me to pay them to return the wrong clutch to me.

review_text: After my last review, I was contacted by Andrew, their Quality Control Manager, who apologized and gave me a €25 voucher. I decided to give them one more chance, and the experience has been even worse.The "Bait-and-Switch" is Systemic: Immediately after my new order, I received the same automated call stating "stock errors" and demanding I pay more for "expensive alternatives." This is not "dynamic pricing"; it is a recurring trap that ignores the price confirmed at checkout.GLS Delivery Failures: The taillight replacement they finally sent has not been delivered to my house. Like clockwork, GLS made no attempt to call or come to my address and simply dumped the package at a collection point. I am now forced to travel to pick up a part I paid to have delivered.Packaging Negligence: I have had two separate shipments destroyed because undercoating tins burst inside the boxes, ruining the entire order.The €25 voucher is just a way to keep you in a broken loop. If you need parts to get a vehicle back on the road, go elsewhere. Auto-doc.pt offers apologies in emails but continues to fail in the real world.I had got into the habit of ordering online, but was pleasantly surprised to have obtained all the parts I needed - some rare - from my local parts store, in one afternoon!
supplier_response: Hello Luis Alves Pereira! We sincerely apologize for the repeated issues you’ve experienced, including pricing confusion, delivery failures, and packaging problems. This is far from the service we aim to provide, and we understand how frustrating and inconvenient this has been. Our Quality Control Manager will be contacting you shortly to review your case and assist you further. Best regards, AUTODOC Team

review_text: Autodoc offers articles at a price, but charges you more at the checkout. It is not dynamic pricing, that is branding for fraudulent behaviour.Then, they email you 5 minutes to tell you that the part you ordered is not available, only a more expensive one, and continue to do the same for other parts on your paid order.When I finally cancelled the order, I was already on my third additional payment to replace parts not in stock. Note: They cannot update their site with live-time existing stock, but can immediately send you an email with updated, more expensive, offers of stock available!In the end they refund you the value advertised initially, not what you paid extra.They also keep your money in your (theirs) "active balance" rather than returning it.I am still waiting for some of those additional payments to be returned to my bank account. To work with them, and GLS, their couriers, is a task in itself where you're more likely to lose money and time than get on with your repairs.
supplier_response: Hello Luis Alves Pereira! We are sorry to hear about your experience and apologize for the inconvenience caused. supplier_response: Hello Manuel Ferreira, We are sorry to hear that the parts you ordered did not fit your car. We strive to ensure that our customers receive only suitable products, and your feedback helps us improve our service. Please note that by registration number you can only limit the list of parts to parts that fit your car model. The final check for compatibility is possible only with the help of the OEN (Original Equipment Number). Before placing an order, you should check the OEN indicated in the description of the item. If the part did not fit, you can arrange a return or exchange in accordance with our policy. You can easily contact us for assistance via live chat or at help@autodoc.de. We can’t see any claims from you concerning this issue. Only one time you had a return request, we got the parts back and refunded you money. Our quality control manager will contact you to clarify more details. Best regards, AUTODOC Team
